title: The 2020 Farm Laws
summary: Three Acts passed in September 2020 to change how farm produce is sold, contracted and stored. Farmer protests followed, and the Acts were repealed in late 2021.
bills: The Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2020
The Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act, 2020
arguments_for: Farmers could sell outside government-run APMC mandis, widening their choice of buyers.
Contract farming could bring private investment and assured buyers.
Relaxing stock limits could attract investment in storage and supply chains.
arguments_against: Farmers feared the mandi system and Minimum Support Price (MSP) procurement would weaken over time.
Small farmers may have little bargaining power against large corporate buyers in contracts.
The bills were passed quickly with limited committee scrutiny, and states, which handle agriculture and markets, were not fully consulted.

choices.label: Vote Aye
choices.outcome: The Acts pass. Large protests build, especially around Delhi's borders, and continue for about a year.

choices.label: Vote Nay
choices.outcome: You vote against. If the majority still carries the bills, the Acts pass without your support, but your dissent is on record.

choices.label: Demand referral to a Select Committee
choices.outcome: You push for detailed scrutiny and consultation with farmer groups and states before any vote. Delay, but a better-tested law.

what_happened: The Acts were passed in September 2020. After sustained protests, the government announced repeal in November 2021, and Parliament repealed them in the Winter Session that year.
